headline.text: Anthropic puts Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides in public beta

slides.altText: Anthropic puts Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides in public beta

headline.text: Claude moves into Google’s office apps

slides.altText: Claude moves into Google’s office apps

body.text: Anthropic says Claude for Google Workspace, a sidebar add-on for Docs, Sheets and Slides, is in public beta on all paid plans. It also released beta connectors to create and edit Google files from Claude chat.

hook.text: Google already has its own AI in these apps. So who is this for?

headline.text: Anthropic is stepping onto Google’s home turf

slides.altText: Anthropic is stepping onto Google’s home turf

body.text: Google’s Gemini AI is already built into Workspace apps. 9to5Google frames the Claude add-on as useful for people who are already invested in Claude.

headline.text: It reads your file, then edits it directly

slides.altText: It reads your file, then edits it directly

body.text: Anthropic says Claude sees the open file and your selection. In Docs it fixes text in place, in Sheets it writes formulas and pivot tables, in Slides it builds slides from the deck’s layouts.

hook.text: An assistant that edits your file directly raises one obvious question: does it ask first?

headline.text: By default, Claude asks before it edits

slides.altText: By default, Claude asks before it edits

body.text: Anthropic says each edit shows up as an approval card in the default mode. Accept all edits skips that, but adding a link, inserting a web image or removing access always pauses.

hook.text: Someone else's file can try to give an AI orders of its own.

headline.text: Anthropic’s answer to hidden instructions in files

slides.altText: Anthropic’s answer to hidden instructions in files: "Claude treats document content as data rather than commands, labels hidden text it finds…" (Anthropic)

body.text: Prompt injection is instructions hidden in someone else’s file that try to make an AI act on them. Anthropic says users should review proposed actions, especially in files from outside their organization.

hook.text: Anthropic also lists limits that can stop a task partway.

quoteText.text: Claude treats document content as data rather than commands, labels hidden text it finds…

headline.text: Google cuts off any single operation at this mark

slides.altText: Google cuts off any single operation at this mark

body.text: Public beta means known limits, Anthropic says. A task can stop partway, and the list includes no reading of Docs comments, direct edits instead of suggestions, and no Firefox.

hook.text: So who is vouching for all of this?

slides.numberNote: Google's limit on a single extension operation; after that a task stops partway

headline.text: Almost everything here is Anthropic’s own word

slides.altText: Almost everything here is Anthropic’s own word

body.text: The sources opened had no independent testing of performance or security. No end date for the beta turned up, and no statement from Google.

caption:
Anthropic has put Claude for Google Workspace, an add-on for Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, into public beta on all paid Claude plans. It also released new beta connectors that let Claude create and edit Google files from the Claude chat, Anthropic says.

Anthropic says the add-on opens in a sidebar beside the file, reads it and can edit it directly. By default each edit waits for the user’s approval, and some actions, such as adding a link or removing access, always pause. Google’s own Gemini is already built into Workspace, and 9to5Google frames the Claude add-on as useful for people already invested in Claude. Anthropic lists beta limits, including a six-minute cap on a single operation and no Firefox support. Most of the capability and security claims come from Anthropic, and the sources opened had no independent testing.

Would you let an AI edit your work files if it asked before every change?
